blocks.html: Restaurant green beans are bright green and crisp-tender, even when served an hour after they were cooked. The trick is blanching and shocking.

Blanch: cook vegetables briefly in a large pot of well-salted, rapidly boiling water. Shock: move them at once into ice water to stop the cooking and set the color. Drain well. Later, they need only a quick reheat in butter or a hot pan.

items: Use plenty of water (many cooks use about a gallon per pound) so the boil comes back fast.
Cook in small batches; leave the lid off for green vegetables.
Taste one: it should bend and still have a little bite.
Blanching also loosens skins (tomatoes, peaches, almonds) and is the first step before freezing many vegetables.

blocks.html: Green comes from chlorophyll. Long cooking, a lid that traps acids from the vegetable, or acid in the water turns it olive-drab. Fast cooking in lots of water, then ice, keeps it bright.

blocks.title: Water
blocks.q: About how much water for 3 pounds of green beans at a gallon per pound?

blocks.html: Blanching a big pile at once. The water stops boiling, the vegetables stew slowly, and they turn dull.

🏠 Practice at home

  • Blanch two batches of green beans: one shocked in ice water, one left to cool on a plate. Compare color and crunch after 30 minutes.
  • Peel tomatoes: score an X, blanch 20 to 30 seconds, shock, and slip off the skins.

blocks.html: Vegetables can be the best thing on the plate. Three methods do most of the work in a restaurant: glazing, roasting and puréeing.

Glaze: cook carrots, turnips or pearl onions in a little water with butter, salt and a pinch of sugar until the water is gone and they are coated in a shiny glaze. Roast: toss in oil and salt, spread on a sheet pan with room between pieces, and roast at high heat (about 400°F to 450°F) until browned at the edges. Purée: cook until very tender, blend with butter or cream, and pass through a fine sieve for a silky texture.

items: Cut evenly so pieces finish together (Knife Skills).
Glaze in a pan just wide enough to hold the vegetables in one layer.
Roast hard vegetables and soft ones separately, or add the soft ones later.
Season purées well; they taste flat without salt and a little acid.

blocks.html: Roasting browns vegetables through the Maillard reaction and caramelization, which needs a dry, hot surface. Crowded on the pan, they release steam and boil instead.

blocks.title: Pick a method
blocks.q: You want carrots that are shiny, tender and lightly sweet, cooked on the stove.
steps: Little liquid, butter, sugar, cooked until the liquid becomes a glaze.

blocks.html: Roasting on a crowded pan at too low a temperature. You get soft, pale vegetables.

🏠 Practice at home

  • Roast cauliflower on two pans: one crowded, one spread out with space. Same oven, same time. Compare.
  • Make a carrot purée and push half through a fine sieve. Taste the difference in texture.

blocks.html: Potatoes come in two basic kinds, and choosing right is half the battle.

Starchy (mealy) potatoes, such as russets, are low in moisture and high in starch: fluffy when baked or mashed, crisp when fried. Waxy potatoes, such as red-skinned and fingerlings, have less starch and more moisture: they hold their shape in salads, soups and gratins. All-purpose potatoes (such as Yukon Gold) sit in between.

items: Mash: start in cold salted water, cook until tender, dry them, then rice or mash; fold in warm butter and milk.
Classic French fries: cut batonnets, rinse off surface starch, fry once at a lower temperature to cook through, rest, then fry again at a higher temperature to crisp.
Gratin: thin even slices (a mandoline with its guard), cream or milk, baked until tender and browned.
Duchess potatoes: puréed potato with yolks, piped and baked.

blocks.html: Potato cells are full of starch granules. Gentle mashing keeps the cells whole; a blender or food processor bursts them and the free starch turns the potatoes gluey.

blocks.title: Pick the potato
blocks.q: Potato salad that keeps its cubes.

blocks.html: Starting potatoes in boiling water. The outside overcooks before the center is done; start them in cold water.

🛡️ Safety

  • Fry with the deep-frying safety rules: dry the potatoes well, small batches, a pot no more than half full of oil, and a lid within reach.

🏠 Practice at home

  • Make mashed potatoes twice: once with russets and a ricer, once with red potatoes and a hand masher. Compare.
  • Make twice-fried fries, and a batch fried once at the higher temperature. Compare.

blocks.html: Rice and grains are cooked three main ways. Risotto is a special case worth learning by itself.

Absorption: a measured amount of liquid, all absorbed (long-grain white rice is often about 1 part rice to 1½ to 2 parts water by volume; check the package). Pilaf: toast the grain in fat with onion, then add hot stock and cook covered. Pasta method: boil in plenty of water and drain (good for brown rice, farro, barley). Risotto: short-grain rice (Arborio, Carnaroli) toasted in butter, then hot stock added a ladle at a time while stirring, about 18 to 20 minutes, until creamy and just tender (all'onda, "like a wave"), finished with butter and Parmesan.
Short-grain risotto rice has lots of a starch that comes off the surface as you stir, thickening the stock into a creamy sauce. Rinsing the rice or adding cold stock works against that.

blocks.title: Scale the water
blocks.q: Your rice uses 1¾ cups of water per cup of rice. How much water for 3 cups of rice?

blocks.html:
🛡️ Safety

  • Cooked rice is a TCS food: cool it quickly by the two-stage rule and keep it cold. Rice left warm for hours can grow germs whose toxins reheating won't remove.
Lifting the lid on absorption rice again and again; the steam escapes and the rice cooks unevenly.

🏠 Practice at home

  • Make a rice pilaf and a plain absorption rice side by side. Taste the difference toasting makes.
  • Make risotto, stirring in hot stock one ladle at a time. Write down how many minutes and how many ladles.

blocks.html: Fresh egg pasta needs only flour, eggs, a work surface and patience.

The ratio: about 100 grams of flour per large egg (an egg is about 50 grams without its shell). Make a well of flour, crack the eggs in, beat them with a fork while drawing in flour, then knead about 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest it, wrapped, 30 minutes. Roll thin (by pin or machine), cut, and cook 1 to 3 minutes in plenty of salted boiling water.

items: Use "00" flour, all-purpose, or a mix with semolina.
Dough too sticky: add flour a spoon at a time. Too dry: wet your hands and knead.
Roll through a machine from the widest setting down, folding and rerolling at the start for strength.
Dust cut pasta with semolina so strands don't stick.

blocks.html: Resting lets the flour finish absorbing the egg and lets the gluten relax, so the dough rolls thin without springing back.

blocks.title: Scale it
blocks.q: How much flour for pasta for 6 people, at 1 egg per person and 100 g flour per egg?

blocks.html: Rolling before resting. The dough fights back and tears.

🏠 Practice at home

  • Make a 2-egg batch of pasta by hand. Cut half into fettuccine and half into pappardelle. Cook one strand to time it before cooking the rest.

blocks.html: Dried beans cost little and taste better than canned when cooked well. They take planning, and one bean takes care.

Sort out stones and broken beans, rinse, and soak beans (overnight in plenty of water, or a quick soak: boil 2 minutes, then rest 1 hour). Drain, cover with fresh water, and simmer until tender. Lentils and split peas need no soaking. Red kidney beans contain a natural toxin destroyed by boiling: soak, drain, and boil hard in fresh water. Meal Prep follows FDA advice to boil for at least 30 minutes.

items: Simmer gently so skins don't burst; stir rarely.
Salt the cooking water to season the beans.
Strong acids (tomato, vinegar) slow softening: add them after the beans are tender.
Old beans may never soften; buy from a store that sells a lot.

blocks.html:
🛡️ Safety

  • Don't cook raw kidney beans in a slow cooker without boiling them first; slow cookers may not get hot enough to destroy the toxin.
Soaking lets water into the bean so it cooks faster and more evenly. The toxin in kidney beans (a lectin) is destroyed by full boiling but not by long cooking at lower temperatures.

blocks.title: Yield
blocks.q: Dried beans roughly triple in volume when cooked. How many cups of cooked beans from 1½ cups dried?

blocks.html: Adding tomatoes at the start of cooking dried beans, so they stay hard for hours.
